source_file: Berlin 2026 edition for next app devCon 2026 (flutterCon Berlin), sources listed on the page
question: Q6: Your Next Move

sections.prompt: Raise your hand if you spent real time this year on a skill outside Flutter: native, backend, product, people.
sections.hint: METR study, Jul 2025: with AI, 16 experienced open-source developers were 19% slower but felt 20% faster; Feb 2026 follow-up: inconclusive. Ask what AI could not shortcut.
no_hands: What is the one deep skill you are betting on?
What would you learn next if you had one free day a week?
For the seniors: which skill paid off most over your career?
hands_up: Did the new skill change what work comes to you?
Did learning it with AI help, or make it shallow?
Was it depth, like native or architecture, or breadth, like product or people?
How do you show that learning to an employer or a client?
follow_ups: What should a Flutter developer still do deliberately by hand?
Which skill pairing with Flutter is underrated right now?

sections.model: An App With Your Name On It
sections.prompt: Raise your hand if an app you built yourself is live in a store or on the web.
sections.hint: Google Play: new personal developer accounts need a closed test with 12 testers for 14 days before production. Ask who hit this hurdle.
no_hands: What stopped you: an idea, time, store hurdles, or no need?
Would a shipped app help you more than a certificate or a course?
For hirers: does a shipped app with real users change how you read a candidate?
hands_up: What did shipping teach you that no tutorial did?
Did it lead to anything: a job, a client, a talk, a lesson?
How much of it would you let an agent build today?
follow_ups: What would you build to show product judgment rather than code generation?

sections.prompt: Raise your hand if you turned down a job or project this year because of its stack.
sections.hint: JetBrains developer survey, Oct 2025: 68% of developers expect employers to require AI-tool skills in the near future. Ask whether AI expectations were behind the no.
no_hands: What would you say yes to outside Flutter: the product, the team, the pay?
How much does the framework matter next to the domain and the people?
For juniors: what would you need to know about a team before saying yes, stack aside?
hands_up: Without naming the company: was the real reason the tech, the team, or the AI expectations?
What do you ask a team now that you did not ask before?
Have you regretted a no, or a yes?
follow_ups: What interview question reveals whether a team uses AI to grow people or to avoid hiring?

wrap_up: Eyes closed again: hands up if you would still choose Flutter starting today. Facilitators count and compare with the worried count from Q1.
One sentence to your past self, from anyone who has been in Flutter for more than two years.
Where does this conversation continue: Flutter Berlin or your local meetup, Flutteristas, the Flutter Community AI Circle, or Friday's native versus cross-platform panel?
